answer: Proof-of-storage-time minting resists sybils: minting requires proving continuous retention of a committed dataset over real elapsed time (storage × duration), re-challenged randomly, binding each identity to sustained physical disk. A dune-wide farm cannot fake held bytes across many identities — each key's proof demands its own retained plot through the challenge window. A falcon-fast attacker gains nothing from speed; the cost is disk held over time per identity, so a vault of thousands needs thousands of distinct plots retained continuously.
